passage:
After Friday prayers, Irfan and Abhinav took their tea to the low wall by the corner stall.
"You told me last week you don't get some of the rules," Abhinav said. "So why go every Friday?"
"Because it's home. Rahim Uncle saves my spot. The boys are there. Ammi's sheer khurma on Eid. When I was small, the smell of that carpet meant safe."
"And the questions?"
"I ask them. I asked our imam about one thing and he said, 'Good question, come Sunday and we'll talk.' He wasn't angry."
"So you don't have to pick."
Irfan turned the glass in his hands. "I keep waiting to be afraid of picking. I'm just not."

qa.q: Who saves Irfan's spot at the mosque?
What is Irfan feeling toward the mosque, and what shows it?
qa.a: Irfan feels belonging and warmth, shown by "it's home" and the memory of the carpet smelling safe, while still holding real questions.

qa.q: What would you advise a friend who wants both belonging and questions?
qa.a: Keep going to the place that feels like home, and ask the questions to an elder or friend who welcomes them, without fearing either.

qa.q: How does Abhinav see Irfan's stance?
qa.a: With curiosity; Abhinav asks why Irfan goes despite the doubts and ends up saying Irfan does not have to pick.

grounding: Irfan finds friends and a sense of home at the mosque and still asks questions, keeping both without fear.
